title: Pharmacology
description: A drug's effect rises with its dose along Hill's curve, E = D^n/(EC₅₀^n + D^n): nothing, then a steep rise, then a plateau. Toxicity follows its own curve at a higher dose; between the two lies the therapeutic window. Dose again before the last has cleared, and the level climbs out of the window. Unlocks the Dose-Response Assay: the Vestibular Suppressant and the Anti-Inflammatory.

puzzle.goal: A drug acts on its receptors with a Hill coefficient n and a half-maximal dose EC₅₀. Write the fraction E of the full effect at dose D.
puzzle.name: The Hill equation
puzzle.form: D ^ n / ( EC50 ^ n + D ^ n )
puzzle.expr: D ^ n / ( EC50 ^ n + D ^ n )
puzzle.ask: Find E for D = @{D} mg, EC₅₀ = @{EC50} mg and n = @{n}.
puzzle.method: n molecules bind at once: occupancy is D^n over the sum of D^n and the dissociation constant EC₅₀^n.
